panels.xlabel: 48 GiB state on four v5e chips

diagram.title: TPU state placement, HBM budget and compute path
diagram.prediction: What remains on each physical chip under replication versus explicit sharding, and where do BF16 operands enter?
diagram.reading: Follow the arrows from the per-device HBM ledger, through operand traffic, into the chosen compute path, and finally to a target trace. The ledger must name placement: for 48 GiB of state on four 16 GiB v5e chips, replication needs 48 GiB/device; ideal even sharding needs 12 GiB/device. With the fixture's 1 GiB activation allowance, that shard needs 13 GiB against 12.8 GiB usable, so it misses by 0.2 GiB. The bandwidth node carries GB/s figures, while the compute comparison is in FLOP/byte; inspect each unit on its own. Inference KV cache is a separate ledger. The next step is to confirm actual sharding and inspect a target trace for memory, compute and communication evidence.
diagram.alt: Conceptual TPU per-device ledger: replicated training state is copied to every chip; explicitly sharded state is partitioned across chips; activations and temporaries use additional HBM; a separate inference path holds KV cache; BF16 operands stream from HBM to compute.

nodes.label: Per-device HBM: replicated or explicitly sharded training state + activations + temporaries; inference KV is a separate case
HBM bandwidth pipe (819-2765 GB/s): stream bf16 / int8 operands
Compute path: explicit operand dtype, accumulation contract and supported lowering
Target trace: inspect compute, memory, transfer and communication evidence
